item.title: Wild beat Bruins 6-2 behind two goals from Ryan Hartman, extending road winning streak to 8 games
item.description: Nov 14, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Minnesota Wild left wing Kirill Kaprizov (97) congratulates right wing Ryan Hartman (38) after scoring a goal during the second period against the Boston Bruins at TD Garden. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect BOSTON — Ryan Hartman and Danila Yurov scored two goals each, Jesper Wallstedt stopped 30 shots, and the Minnesota Wild beat the Boston Bruins 6-2 on Saturday night to extend their road winning streak to eight games. Kirill Kaprizov extended his point streak to 11 games (six goals, 14 assists) with two assists for the West-leading Wild, who have earned at least a point in 11 straight games (9-0-2). Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman scored 67 seconds apart in the opening two minutes of the second period for Minnesota, which cruised to its NHL-best 10th road victory. Yurov scored both of his in the third period, the second an empty-netter. David Pastrnak and Fraser Minten scored for Boston, which lost its second straight home game after winning seven in a row at TD Garden. Both losses came wearing their new mostly brown “varsity jerseys” with bright yellow numbers, trim and helmets that they debuted Thursday. After getting pulled in Boston’s lopsided loss at home against Montreal Thursday — its first at home since Oct. 5 — Jeremy Swayman started and made 19 saves. Hartman’s first came on a wrister from the left circle that beat Swayman inside the far post, making it 1-0 at 6:54 of the opening period. Hughes slipped a wrister past Swayman 53 seconds into the middle period and Coleman’s slap shot from the point found its way past a few bodies and into the net, making it 3-0. Minten’s power-play goal came at 8:45 but Hartman’s second took away Boston’s brief momentum 75 seconds later. The Wild won the first meeting of the season , 4-1, at home on Oct. 3 when Kaprizov scored two goals. The teams entered tied with the NHL’s second-best goal differential (plus-24) behind Carolina.

item.title: Seahawks avoid travel issues for Raiders game following nationwide ground stop
item.description: It’s been a hectic weekend for airline travel after apparent equipment issues resulted in a nationwide ground stop on Friday. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) did lift the order after four hours, but the resulting chaos was thousands of canceled and rescheduled flights, which continued into Saturday. Luckily, while college sports were significantly impacted by the sudden travel issues, the Seattle Seahawks were able to head to Las Vegas to take on the Raiders as originally scheduled. The Seahawks are en route to Las Vegas right now as planned, so no changes to their travel schedule. — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 14, 2026 It sure helps to have a charter flight in this scenario. For shorter trips like Seattle to Las Vegas, the Seahawks will typically travel on a Saturday, whereas cross-country trips like their Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders have involved Friday departures. The NFL is probably fortunate that not a single Week 10 Sunday matchup has a Pacific Time Zone team playing in the Eastern Time Zone (or vice versa). College football and basketball games were rescheduled throughout the country as a result of Friday’s outage, with the Washington Huskies men’s basketball matchup with Utah postponed outright to December due to additional travel problems . Huskies football did fly to Michigan on Friday night but still had their kickoff against Michigan State moved back by an hour. The NFL didn’t come away from the travel nightmare unscathed, as several games will have makeshift officiating crews. Side judge Don Willard will be the head referee for the Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts at 10 am PT, then drive to Cincinnati to ref the Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football at 5:20 pm PT. Unfortunately, some fans hoping to go to Vegas for a weekend to catch some Seahawks football had their dreams dashed, as we documented on Friday .

item.title: Real Madrid tipped to complete first signing of 2027 for just €9 million
item.description: Real Madrid tipped to complete first signing of 2027 for just €9 million Real Madrid are already looking towards the summer 2027 transfer window as the club seek to strengthen the squad at Jose Mourinho’s disposal. The signings they made in 2026 have worked out very well so far, with each player finding a way to contribute to Mourinho’s team. One player who could feature prominently in their 2027 plans is Jacobo Ramon, who has developed remarkably since leaving the Santiago Bernabeu for Como in 2025. Real Madrid planning €9 million move for Jacobo Ramon According to journalist Miguel Serrano, speaking on his YouTube channel, Los Blancos are increasingly convinced that they should bring the academy graduate back next summer. “Real Madrid are clear that they have to bring Jacobo back,” Serrano explained, suggesting that the defender could become the club’s first signing ahead of the 2027/28 campaign (h/t Defensa Central ). Madrid possess a buy-back option worth approximately €9 million, having initially sold the youngster to Como for €2.5 million. Real Madrid want to bring back Jacobo Ramon to the club. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Serrano admitted that his opinion of Ramon has changed considerably since watching him against Leganes during Carlo Ancelotti’s final season. “He has grown under Fabregas, become an undisputed starter and is now a senior international,” the journalist explained. The 21-year-old’s performances in Italy have established him as one of the most promising young defenders in European football. Mourinho could have room for another centre-back Ramon could return as the fourth-choice centre-back, competing for minutes alongside Dean Huijsen, Ibrahima Konate and Eder Militao. Antonio Rudiger is also expected to stay for another season, but considering his age, he is unlikely to feature regularly for the team. Ramon could take up Rudiger’s place in the squad. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Ramon could come in and provide Mourinho with a high-quality option in a position where the right balance is always crucial. Alternatively, should the club feel they do not have space in their squad, they could buy him and then sell him back to Como. This is a trick Los Blancos pulled off quite neatly with Nico Paz this past summer, and they can do the same with Ramon. Regardless, Real Madrid signing Ramon seems like a given at this stage, and it remains to be seen how things play out.

item.title: The relentless rise of Jason Cundy: How a forgotten footballer became UK sports radio's most popular wind-up merchant
item.description: Jason Cundy GFX - GOAL/talkSPORT The 56-year-old former Chelsea defender is on a 'generational run', going viral on a near-weekly basis for his antics on talkSPORT Younger football fans could be forgiven for not having heard of Jason Cundy until a few years ago. A playing career that had so much promise would drift into relative obscurity after his time at Chelsea and Tottenham in the 90s, and he was even forced into early retirement. Now, though, he is going viral across social media on a near-weekly basis for his on-air antics. Cundy is a talkSPORT stalwart after more than 20 years with the radio station, but his emergence as a master wind-up merchant has seen his popularity soar. In fact, the 56-year-old's 'generational run' means there there is an argument he should be sweeping sports broadcasting awards in 2026. Chelsea, survival & early retirement Cundy started his career at Chelsea before going on to play for Tottenham, but his playing days were hampered by a series of health problems While he is now arguably more synonymous with being a broadcaster after more than 20 years in the business, Cundy actually enjoyed a top-level professional playing career that incorporated spells at Chelsea and, ironically, their London rivals Tottenham, whom he now spends a significant chunk of his time tearing into. A lifelong Chelsea fan who used to watch the Blues at Stamford Bridge as a boy, the tough-tackling centre-back came through the club's academy in the 80s, earning their Young Player of the Year award in 1987. He spent four years in the first team in west London before being sold to Spurs in 1992. Hampered by persistent fitness issues throughout his career, Cundy was forced to be patient for opportunities at White Hart Lane and headed on various loans before permanent spells with Ipswich Town and Portsmouth. It was during his time with the latter that the defender was diagnosed with testicular cancer in early 1997, undergoing surgery to remove one of his testicles and eventually making a full recovery, returning to the pitch later that year. However, his playing days would be curtailed three years later. In December 2000, aged just 31, he was forced to retire on medical advice following a serious knee injury that he had actually suffered in training when he was still an Ipswich player, with his final appearance coming almost a year prior on Boxing Day 1999. "I haven't put my boots on since that game at Swindon," Cundy said at the time. "I cleaned them after the game, put them in the boot of my car - and they've been there ever since. It's a sad day. I'm now an ex-pro footballer. When I signed as a 17-year-old for Chelsea, I never imagined it would ever come to this." item.title: Bundesliga defender not a viable option for Barcelona despite recent links – report
item.description: Bundesliga defender not a viable option for Barcelona despite recent links – report Last week, it was reported that Jonathan Tah has emerged as a potential candidate for Barcelona as they look to shore up their ranks in the defensive unit in January. The club have struggled with injuries in the defensive department, with the likes of Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen, Jules Kounde, and Xavi Espart all picking up injuries at some form or the other. This has led Barcelona to reportedly consider a move for Bayern Munich star Tah, who is a key defender for both his club and country. Tah not an option for Barcelona Jonathan Tah is a key player for German national team. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) However, a recent report from Diario SPORT has now clarified that Tah is not a serious option for Barcelona. This is largely because Bayern Munich are not willing to consider the sale of the German international, while the player himself is not too keen on leaving the club either. Therefore, a Barcelona move for Tah has been practically ruled out, even though the club are interested in acquiring the services of the former Bayer Leverkusen star. It must be noted that Barça were one of the contenders to sign Tah when he had decided to run out his contract at Leverkusen in 2025. Ultimately, Bayern Munich won the race to his signature. No change of air required Tah believes Bayern is the place to be. (Photo by Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images) The report points out that Barcelona do have an excellent relationship with Tah’s agent, Pini Zahavi. The Israeli agent is the representative of Hansi Flick and shares a good bond with Joan Laporta, having previously helped the club sign Robert Lewandowski as well. However, Tah is simply not willing to leave Bayern Munich, having already established himself as a key player at the back, with 67 appearances in all competitions since joining the club. Now a regular in the German team as well, Tah is currently at the peak of his powers and believes Bayern is the place to be. Barcelona, for their part, are aware of Tah’s lack of desire to switch clubs and therefore, are likely to shift their focus onto other potential targets in the market.

item.title: Terry Butcher compares Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane to 1966 World Cup hero Bobby Moore and backs striker to lead England to Euro 2028 glory
item.description: England v Croatia - UEFA Nations League 2026/27 Group A3 MD5 - Getty Images Sport Former England captain Terry Butcher has likened Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane to 1966 World Cup-winning skipper Bobby Moore after the striker broke the nation's all-time appearance record. Following Thursday's milestone outing against Croatia at Wembley, the ex-defender has backed the forward to lead the Three Lions to Euro 2028 glory. Former skipper hails record-breaking striker Butcher believes the 33-year-old striker commands the same respect as England's only World Cup-winning captain and can end the country's major trophy wait on home soil in two years' time. Present at Wembley on Thursday to collect his own legacy cap, the former centre-back watched Kane celebrate his recent Ballon d'Or triumph by becoming England's most-capped men's player . The forward marked the occasion by converting the winning penalty in a 2-1 UEFA Nations League victory over Croatia. Model professional leads by example Speaking to the Press Association about Kane's leadership and longevity ahead of the 2028 finals co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland from June 9 to July 9, Butcher said: "I think he is terrific. He's playing some of the best football of his career now. He's relaxed, he's fit, he looks strong, he's got a fantastic attitude. He's looked after by really nice people. "He lives the right way, behaves the right way, plays the right way. He's a model professional. For me, he just resembles Bobby Moore in terms of how people look up to him. "He is a different type of player to me, he's a striker, and I was a centre back and most people prefer someone at the back or in midfield to be captain, but he leads by example. He does the right things and he's someone that has a strong mentality. He's someone that wants it and well respected. "He's still got life in him, we still want him to get more caps, we still want him to get more goals. The World Cup might be just too far away, but the Euros are certainly within the realms of possibility that he can captain England there. I certainly hope so." Home tournament offers golden opportunity After reaching the last two European Championship finals and claiming bronze at this summer's World Cup - their third semi-final since 1966 following the 1990 run when Butcher wore the armband - the ex-defender feels only a mental barrier remains: "It is a mentality in terms of we've been there before and we haven't got over, but you've got to just dismiss that. "There's a big hump or a big chasm, once you get over that, you're on the other side, it's like, 'wow, this is the promised land.' But I think I think they're well placed [to win it]. It'd be great to be at home, in front of our home crowd and it's perfectly set up for us to do that now. We've got to take advantage of that." item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Georgia Tech WR coach DeAndre Hopkins has perfect reaction to beating alma mater Clemson appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets pulled off a stunning upset of the Clemson Tigers on Saturday, and no one enjoyed it more than wide receivers coach DeAndre Hopkins . Georgia Tech dominated Clemson 20-6 at Memorial Stadium, and Hopkins was all smiles as he celebrated the victory after the game. The moment was made even sweeter by the fact that it came against his alma mater, where he starred as a wide receiver from 2010 to 2012. “It’s happening! It’s about to happen! It’s happening!,” Hopkins said in a clip posted by KingSZN on X, which was originally posted on Instagram. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Georgia Tech WR Coach DeAndre Hopkins celebrating the win over Clemson 😭🔥 Hopkins played WR for Clemson from 2010-2012 (🎥 lamiless on IG) pic.twitter.com/RqCWOvUjcb — KingSZN (@King_Szn10) November 14, 2026 Hopkins joined the Yellow Jackets’ staff in July as an assistant wide receivers coach before being promoted to lead the position group for the final three games of the regular season . Saturday’s trip to Death Valley marked his first game in the new role, and it could not have gone much better. The five-time All-Pro, who spent 13 seasons in the NFL with the Houston Texans, Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans, Kansas City Chiefs and Baltimore Ravens, watched his team control the game from start to finish . Georgia Tech leaned heavily on its ground game, piling up a season-high 269 rushing yards. Justice Haynes led the way with 116 yards, including a 53-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. Grady Adamson added a career-high 87 rushing yards and a score. The Yellow Jackets’ defense was just as impressive, holding Clemson to 228 total yards and keeping the Tigers out of the end zone. Clemson also lost starting quarterback Tait Reynolds to a knee injury on the opening drive. The win was Georgia Tech’s first at Clemson since 2008, snapping an eight-game losing streak at Death Valley. The Yellow Jackets improved to 3-7 on the season, while Clemson fell to 6-4. Georgia Tech will look to carry the momentum into next Saturday’s home game against Wake Forest. item.title: Arch Manning makes a triumphant Louisiana return vs LSU in Week 11
item.description: BATON ROUGE – LSU football found itself in another dogfight against a ranked opponent inside Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. With the Tigers hosting No. 8 Texas in a must-win matchup if they wanted to sniff the College Football Playoff in their first season with Lane Kiffin at the helm, containing the Longhorns star quarterback Arch Manning at the top of the LSU defense's to-do list. For most of the game, it did just that. He threw a season-high three interceptions and it looked like LSU had his number. But in the final two minutes, no one could stand in the way of Manning and victory as he willed Texas to a 22-21 comeback win. He used his legs to bring the Longhorns just shy of the goal line with just 13 seconds left on the clock. And, in a state where his football career started, he made more history, throwing a 4-yard touchdown pass to secure Texas' eighth win of the season. “I think in a bunch of years from now, I’m gonna tell everyone I had a game-winning drive and everyone’s gonna forget the three picks,” Manning joked during his postgame news conference. “I mean, it’s Death Valley at night, 2-minute drive. Let’s go.” Arch Manning never backs down For most of the Week 11 matchup, it was far from the return Manning would’ve hoped for in his first collegiate game in Louisiana. Every pass was contested and any yards gained on the ground were hard fought for Texas’ offense. The Archbishop Newman alum looked rattled to start the game. Before his game-winning 4-yard touchdown pass to Raleek Brown in the final seconds of the game, Manning hadn’t found the end zone at all. “It hadn’t been great all night, so I figured it was time to go get it done,” Manning said. “I grew up around a lot of LSU fans, so it feels good to come back for Mardi Gras or come back whenever I come home and not have them talk a bunch of crap.” Manning remained level-headed in the game despite getting sacked four times. He went on to throw for 174 yards while completing close to 55% of his passes. But this victory wasn’t about Manning looking like the better signal caller. It was all about grit. “It was hard, it was tough and he (Manning) had to use his legs,” Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said. “He got sacked, took some sacks, made some tough throws. But what a drive at the end of the game to shake all that off and to make some of the throws he made. He competed at a really high level tonight. “So I was proud of him, and what a moment for him. Being back in his home state and winning this game the way that it was won.” With this victory, Texas has closed the door for LSU and its dreams for making the College Football Playoffs. For Manning, the win is a little extra sweet as he can join the list of other Mannings who come to Death Valley and left victorious. item.title: Jackson Arnold sparks fourth quarter comeback as UNLV upsets New Mexico
item.description: UNLV Rebels quarterback Jackson Arnold (11) scrambles during a game against the New Mexico Lobos at University Stadium in Albuquerque, NM, on Nov. 14, 2026. ALBUQUERQUE—The UNLV Rebels might not have had the season expected of a Mountain West favorite, but they had zero issue playing the role of College Football Playoff spoiler. On Saturday, UNLV put together one of their most inspired efforts of the season, surprising the current Mountain West leading New Mexico Lobos 21-14 to all but dash the conference’s hopes of landing the Group of 6 CFP berth. It was far from smooth sailing for UNLV, however, as they had expected difficulties against one of the best defenses in the nation. Quarterback Jackson Arnold only had 49 passing yards in the first half and was subbed out for Alex Orji on occasion. He was also responsible for two turnovers in New Mexico territory, as UNLV sputtered to only seven points through three quarters. However, with the Rebels down 14 at the end of the third quarter, Arnold and the offense came alive at a crucial time. After the defense forced New Mexico to punt on Arnold’s second turnover, he would lead an efficient drive downfield, ending with a 43-yard touchdown pass to Kayden McGee to cut the lead down to one possession. On the next drive, Arnold would secure another big play on a 44-yard touchdown run to give UNLV their first lead of the game with seven and a half minutes to go. However, the Rebels would need their defense to come up large, and the maligned unit put together a quality effort. While the Rebels did allow 203 rushing yards to continue the struggles against the run, they were able to take advantage of a Lobos team down on its luck at the quarterback position. Linebacker Cam Santee was responsible for one of three sacks, as well as leading the Rebels with 12 tackles (2.5 for loss). Andre Porter and Elias Rudolph recorded the other sacks. However, UNLV’s biggest play would come on the final New Mexico drive, as cornerback Tony-Louis Nkuba was able to record the game-winning interception for their sole turnover of the game. With their sixth victory on the season, the Rebels secured bowl eligibility for the fourth consecutive season, which becomes a new program record. UNLV now has a chance to secure some real momentum heading into their bowl game, finishing off their road schedule against San Jose State next Saturday.

item.description: Ethan says his daughter Aoibheann's confidence has grown since she took up playing boccia [BBC] Growing up Aoibheann struggled to find a sports club to join. Now, she plays boccia, a game designed for those with disabilities, and is beating several of her classmates. Dad Ethan said the "opportunity for Aoibheann to have something of her own to do, that's just for her" makes such a difference. The pair were taking part in a Junior Paralympic fun day aimed at showcasing several sports for those with a physical disability. It allows young people to try out different sports such as powerchair football, wheelchair tennis, wheelchair cycling, golf and boccia. Ethan says that out of the sports available boccia is "probably her favourite", adding it gives Aoibheann confidence. In boccia, the aim is for each team or individual to throw their ball closest to the white ball. It is similar to pétanque. "There isn't a lot of clubs and social gatherings that Aoibheann has an opportunity to take part in," he says. But boccia also allows her to play with her sisters, as they can use manual wheelchairs to take part in the game. "They all play together so it's a level playing field and it's just lovely to see them playing together where Aoibheann is fully involved in the game and it's not kind of segregated in anyway." item.title: Gane, Harrison retain titles in historic night at UFC 334
item.description: Nov 14, 2026; New York, New York, UNITED STATES; Ciryl Gane (red gloves) fights Josh Hokit (blue gloves) in a heavyweight title bout during UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden. NEW YORK CITY — Madison Square Garden hosted UFC 334 on Saturday night, with two championship matchups headlining a card that delivered a memorable retirement performance, a fast finish over one of the promotion’s most durable veterans and an unusual majority draw. Few venues in sports carry the fight history of Madison Square Garden. From Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier's legendary 1971 "Fight of the Century" to decades of championship boxing, the Garden has long been one of combat sports' most iconic stages. The UFC made its long-awaited debut at the venue in November 2016 with UFC 205, headlined by Conor McGregor's historic victory over Eddie Alvarez. Ten years later, UFC 334 marked the promotion's 10th event inside the Garden, adding another chapter to the building's storied fight history. Ciryl Gane def. Josh Hokit via unanimous decision (48-47 x3) Gane retained his heavyweight championship after five hard fought rounds, earning a unanimous decision on all three judges' scorecards. The fight delivered an extraordinary display of heavyweight striking, with both men setting records for significant strikes. The bout opened at a frenetic pace rarely seen among the division's biggest fighters. Gane landed precise uppercuts and jabs, while Hokit answered with a barrage of punches and refused to let off the gas. The second round continued at a heavy-metal, breakneck pace, with both fighters trading shots and showing little interest in slowing down. After 10 minutes of nonstop action, both warriors were wearing damage. The Madison Square Garden crowd responded with chants of "USA." The action finally had to slow down in the third round, if only slightly. Hokit continued pressing forward and landing shots, while Gane countered effectively, defended takedown attempts and worked elbows into the clinch. item.description: ONTARIO, CA. -- Francesco Pinelli tallies two goals in the Ontario Reign 5-2 win against the Abbotsford Canucks. It’s been 10 days since the Reign were last on home ice and last weekend Ontario played two games in Abbotsford. And yet Ontario has allowed only four goals in the past three games against the Canucks. “I think we defended really well,” Ontario coach Andrew Lord said. “Didn’t give up much off the rush, which they’re (Abbotsford) lethal in. And (Erik Portillo) was really good here tonight.” Portillo finished with 23 saves and Abbotsford goalie Nikita Tolopilo ended with 25 saves on 30 shots. Following a hooking penalty by Henry Brzustewicz, the Reign had their first penalty kill of the night in which Pinelli scored a shorthanded goal; setting the tone for the rest of the game. But the Canucks wouldn’t let their power play opportunity pass them by. Kirill Kudryavtsev and Braeden Cootes assisted Chase Wouters in his game-tying power-play goal. The Cleveland Cavaliers took care of business against the Dallas Mavericks on Saturday night, but one of the best moments of the night came when Kyrie Irving , who received a warm welcome in his return to Cleveland, and James Harden shared a reunion of their own. During Cleveland’s 127-117 win at Rocket Arena, Irving and Harden, who sat out the game , were spotted catching up. item.title: Chelsea maintain interest in Real Betis winger Jose Antonio Morante
item.description: Chelsea maintain interest in Real Betis winger Jose Antonio Morante Chelsea remain interested in Real Betis youngster Jose Antonio Morante after exploring a potential move for the winger during the summer, but the 19-year-old is determined to establish himself at his boyhood club. The Premier League side have followed Morante’s development for several years and stepped up their interest after his impressive performances at the UEFA European Under-19 Championship, which Spain won last summer. Morante finished as the tournament’s joint-top scorer with four goals and earned a place in the Team of the Tournament. According to ABC de Sevilla , Chelsea approached the player’s representatives to discuss the possibility of a transfer. Although a move was considered, no formal offer was made, with Morante choosing to remain in Seville and pursue his ambition of becoming a regular in the Betis first team. The Spanish club moved to secure his future after the tournament, extending his contract until June 2030. His new agreement includes a €30 million release clause. Chelsea remain interested in Real Betis youngster Jose Antonio Morante Morante has already had opportunities to work with Manuel Pellegrini’s senior squad, although regular playing time remains limited. He has featured in two La Liga matches and one Champions League fixture this season, making an impression despite his relatively brief appearances. He scored in Betis’ victory over Osasuna and also played a part in the comeback against Elche, with his effort hitting the post before Riquelme converted the rebound. His late involvement against Borussia Dortmund provided another opportunity to demonstrate his potential. Competition for attacking places remains considerable. Antony and Abde are currently ahead in the wide positions, while Pellegrini has also used several other players across the flanks. Morante’s ability to operate on either side, despite preferring the right, gives the manager additional tactical options. An untimely hip injury has temporarily interrupted his progress, ruling him out of the Copa del Rey fixture against Navalcarnero and raising doubts over his availability for the derby against Sevilla. Chelsea’s interest has reportedly remained persistent, but Morante’s immediate priority is earning a more prominent role at Betis. With his contract secured until 2030, the Spanish club are well placed to protect one of their most promising young talents. LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin gave credit where it was due after Saturday night’s heartbreaking 22-21 loss to the Texas Longhorns in Baton Rouge. Still, watching a two-score lead slip through his fingers in Death Valley left a bitter taste in his mouth. Kiffin praised Texas for executing in the clutch after quarterback Arch Manning fired a 4-yard touchdown pass to running back Raleek Brown with three seconds left. Yet the first-year LSU coach did not hide his frustration over letting a winnable SEC showdown get away. “Really disappointing to be up two scores in the game and not being able to close it out. Plenty of opportunities, even with all the stuff before. … We outplayed them to win the game, but that’s not how it works. Disappointed for our players, our fans,” Kiffin said postgame. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lane Kiffin credits Texas for the win. But he’s disappointed in how Texas was able to make the game-winning play. #LSU pic.twitter.com/808NkcFN0h — Cory Diaz (@ByCoryDiaz) November 15, 2026 The box score backs up Kiffin’s point. No. 24 LSU outgained No. 8 Texas 366-273 in total offense and averaged 5.5 yards per play compared to Texas’ 4.1. Running back Dilin Jones gashed the Longhorns for 125 rushing yards on 19 carries, including a 44-yard touchdown burst late in the third quarter that gave the Tigers a commanding 21-10 cushion. Quarterback Sam Leavitt threw for 244 yards and two touchdowns, connecting with wide receiver Jackson Harris eight times for 64 yards and both scores, while wideout Eugene Wilson III hauled in seven passes for 96 yards. However, those missed opportunities Kiffin mentioned proved fatal. LSU went just 2-for-5 in the red zone, missed a 38-yard field goal before halftime and watched Leavitt throw three interceptions to Texas defensive back Jelani McDonald. Even though LSU’s defense intercepted Manning three times and held him to 174 passing yards, the Longhorns capitalized on every break, going 4-for-4 in the red zone. Now sitting at 6-4 overall and 3-4 in SEC play, Kiffin and the Tigers are left wondering what could have been.
